## Construction repairs recorded in this pass

1. **B-page dependency rule (b-leaf).** Five declared dependencies pointed at
   published items homed only on examples pages
   (`ex-one-point-compactifications-of-the-line-and-of-the-naturals`,
   `ex-pontryagin-dual-of-euclidean-space`,
   `ex-normalized-haar-measure-on-a-finite-group`,
   `ex-pontryagin-dual-of-the-integers-is-the-circle`,
   `ex-unitary-dual-and-full-group-c-star-algebra-of-the-integers`). SCHEMA
   forbids using a B-page-only item as another page's dependency. Repairs:
   the compact-metrizability of P¹(ℝ) is now proved locally by the explicit
   inverse-stereographic homeomorphism ℝ* → S¹ with A-homed published
   suppliers; the dual of ℝ² is identified through the published A-homed
   character/product-dual lemmas; finite-group Haar measure uses the published
   A-homed normalized-Haar-probability corollary with the counting measure
   checked directly; the ℤ counterexample constructs its characters directly.
   After the repair, `validate-plan` (whole plan, this manifest spliced) exits 0
   with no `b-leaf`, `undeclared-prereq`, `resolve`, `forward-ref` or
   `intra-order` errors for this batch.
2. **Weak-containment equivalence scope.** The published
   `lem-weak-containment-of-the-trivial-representation-and-almost-invariant-vectors`
   is stated for locally compact Hausdorff groups and its own remark proves
   that the general-topological-group equivalence fails. The scaffold now
   restricts the `1_G ≺ π` identification in
   `def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unitary-representation` and
   `def-spectral-gap-for-a-unitary-representation` to the locally compact
   Hausdorff case (recording that only the direction from almost invariant
   vectors holds in general), and
   `thm-property-t-is-uniform-spectral-gap-for-representations` states the
   spectral-gap identification for locally compact Hausdorff groups while its
   displacement-bound iff is kept for all topological groups.
3. **GNS-converse form.** The final sentence of
   `lem-almost-invariant-vectors-and-positive-type-functions` claimed that
   *each* GNS representation of a net of positive-type functions converging to
   1 on compacta itself has almost invariant vectors. That is false for a
   single member of such a net (e.g. a net that eventually converges and has
   one non-amenable regular-representation member). The statement now asserts
   the correct net form — eventual `(Q,ε)`-invariance of the cyclic vectors,
   hence almost invariant vectors of the Hilbert direct sum — with the direct
   sum added to the dependencies and the caveat in the strategy.
4. **Isolation theorem escalated, not weakened.** See the unresolved findings.
5. **Amenable-plus-(T) route.** The design's prose suggests combining Hulanicki
   with isolation of the trivial representation; the scaffold instead proves
   the theorem directly (Hulanicki gives almost invariant vectors of λ_G, (T)
   gives a nonzero invariant vector, the locally proved finite-Haar-volume
   criterion gives compactness). This is a deliberate route choice that avoids
   consuming the held isolation theorem; the statement (KHV Theorem 1.1.6) is
   unchanged.

def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unita.reason: Definition: (Q,eps)-invariant vectors and almost invariant vectors with the uniform-on-compacts quantifiers, from Bekka-de la Harpe-Valette Definition 1.1.1 and Breuillard PCMI Lecture 2 Sec. II (fetched full texts: KHV 523 pp sha256_16 0281823290dfb42e; Breuillard 38 pp 7272f3b62d2ee7cd). Scaffold repair during construction: the identification with 1_G weakly contained in pi is now quoted only under the locally compact Hausdorff hypothesis of the published lem-weak-containment-of-the-trivial-representation-and-almost-invariant-vectors, whose own remark proves the converse fails for general topological groups; the item records the direction that does hold in general. All dependencies are published items on published pages; no in-run dependency.

def-kazhdan-pair-and-kazhdan-constant.reason: Definition: Kazhdan pairs/sets, displacement constant kappa(G,Q,pi) and Kazhdan constant kappa(G,Q), from KHV Definition 1.1.3 and Remark 1.1.4 (fetched full text, sha256_16 0281823290dfb42e). Checked the two elementary identifications claimed in the item: (Q,eps) is a Kazhdan pair iff kappa(G,Q) >= eps (monotonicity in eps plus the interval structure), and kappa(G,Q,pi) >= kappa(G,Q) for every representation without nonzero invariant vector. Dependency def-almost-invariant-vectors is the only in-run one (level 0); the rest are published.

def-kazhdans-property-t.reason: Definition: property (T) via almost invariant vectors, for topological groups; the compact-Kazhdan-set formulation is delegated to the in-run thm-property-t-is-equivalent-to-the-existence-of-a-kazhdan-pair (level 2). Sources: KHV Definition 1.1.3 and Remark 1.1.2, Breuillard Lecture 2 Sec. II, read in the fetched full texts. All deps published except def-almost-invariant-vectors; the two displayed formulations are definitionally identical.

lem-sl2-r-has-no-invariant-probability-o.reason: Lemma: no Borel probability on P^1(R) is invariant under two unipotents with distinct fixed lines, in particular u_+ and u_- (Breuillard Exercises Sec. 2 III.5, read in the fetched full text). Deps published plus the in-run def-real-projective-line (level 0).

prop-sl2-r-does-not-have-property-t.reason: Proposition: SL2(R) fails (T) via the spherical complementary series I_{0,nu}. The batch-3 corollary (level 9) gives phi_nu -> 1 uniformly on compacta as nu approaches 1, so the K-fixed vector f_0 is (Q,eps)-invariant for nu close to 1; the batch-3 K-type decomposition shows K-fixed vectors are exactly the multiples of f_0, and the batch-3 compact-picture cocycle formula at (k=e, g=a_t) gives (a_t.f_0)(e) = |alpha(a_t)|^{1-nu} != 1, so no nonzero multiple of f_0 is G-invariant. Hence no compact (Q,eps) is a Kazhdan pair and, by the in-run Kazhdan-pair equivalence, (T) fails. Deps: batch-3 items def-normalized-principal-series (level 1), thm-compact-picture (2), lem-k-type-decomposition (3), thm-unitarity (8), cor-convergence (9); otherwise published.
